notes:
### New

- The catacombs go down three levels, one under the other. The far end of the first and second levels has a way out and a great barred double door: hold E (X on a controller) to open it, and a long stair takes you down. It's the only way down, and once it's open, whatever is below can come up.
- The Gloaming is a real fight now. Performing the rite is what brings it, right there in the chapel, and it's only resolved once you banish it. Then you still have to get out past whatever else is down there.
- The Gloaming rears back before it strikes, so you can see the blow coming and step out of reach. A blow hurts but doesn't drop you outright, and what you wear takes some of it. It burns brighter the longer you hold a lamp on it, and flares when weapons can hurt it.
- Flick your headlamp off and on with the Gloaming in the beam and the flash stuns it for 2 seconds. It won't fall for it again for 20.
- The fight with the Gloaming has its own music, from the moment the rite brings it until you banish it, and you hear its blow coming.
- Ropes. The shafts out at the end of the first and second levels are ropes you climb: look at one and press E (X) to take hold, climb with forward and back, hold Shift to climb faster or slide down, and let go with C (B). Nobody can climb past someone else on the same rope.
- Rope packs, 100 metres for 50 in the store, and the odd rope bundle in a crate. Hold attack and walk to lay rope behind you and find your way back. Hold E on a laid rope to gather it up and get it back.
- The Drop and The Pit, rooms that fall away 12 metres. Tie a rope at the post at the top (hold E) and the whole party can climb down to the crates at the bottom, and back up. Nobody can untie it while someone is on it.
- Draw your own map. Buy a surveyor's notebook in the store, carry it down, and press M (or Map in your pack) to open it. Stand still and hold Sketch to draw what you can see around you; stand next to a friend and hold Show to swap what you both know.
- A menu underground: Tab or I (View on a controller) opens your pack, with a Rite tab beside it that shows what you know of the rite and who carries what. Abandon expedition is there now too. While it's open your hands are full: you can walk, but not fight or use things.
- Choose the eight chalk marks on your wheel from the Loadout page. Thirteen new ones to pick from, all free: Loot, Trap, Water, Way out, Stairs, Wait here, Meet here, Creature, Safe, Locked, Crate, Help and Someone fell.
- Avatars: upload a picture on the Account screen and frame it in the circle. It shows beside your gamer tag and to your party. Signed in with Discord? Your Discord avatar is used until you upload your own.
- Medkits: rare, 50 in the store, and they give back all your sanity at once.
- Bigger rooms: a pillared charnel vault and long burial galleries lined with niches.
- Run diagnostics, in the account menu: if the game runs slowly for you, it walks through the same stretch of catacombs at each graphics quality, takes about a minute, and lets you send us the frame rates so we can make it run better on machines like yours.
- Sounds above ground: the menus click and tick as you move through them, and a quiet ambience plays under the dashboard.
- The game has its logo on the sign-in page and its own icon in your browser tab and on your home screen.
- On the Expedition page, the Affliction you've chosen sits wreathed in drifting smoke.

### Changes

- Teammate lamp shadows, in Settings > Graphics: if the game slows down in a full party, set it to Nearest or Off. Your teammates' lamps cast fewer shadows, though a lamp without shadows shines through walls.
- Falls hurt. Drop from high up and you lose sanity and are hobbled for 20 seconds, no faster than a crawl. Anything wrong with you like this shows beside your health, with the seconds left.
- The good loot is deeper: crates on the first two levels hold everyday things, and anything rare or precious is on the third, where the rite is done.
- The creatures are tougher, more so the bigger your party.
- The Gloaming no longer turns up because you've stayed too long, and being near it no longer drains you. The red arrival bar under the clock is gone, and so is the red at the edges of the screen when your sanity runs low.
- Under the water the view turns murky green. Once you dive you stay at the depth you swim to until you swim back up or run out of breath, and you can't swim hard or fight under the water.
- Squeezes are much longer, and there's no room to fight in one, nor while crawling.
- The headlamp key: tap F (D-pad up) to switch it off and on again, and hold it for a second to change between low and bright.
- Hide the rite down the left of the screen with H (a click of the right stick), and bring it back the same way. Your party's health always stays on screen.
- No more passages that leave a room and wander straight back into it.
- The results screen's deepest level counts the three levels.
- Hold the cursor over anything in the store to see what it is and what it does.
- The game's fonts now come from the game itself, so nothing about you is sent to Google to show them.

### Controllers

- Shortcuts on the dashboard, with their buttons on screen: hold X to launch an expedition and again to confirm your loadout, hold Y for the store or to purchase, View for your Loadout, a click of the right stick for Social, and LB and RB for the tabs.
- In the store, choose how many with the right stick, and the left stick goes straight to Purchase.
- In a crate or on a corpse, once X has sent an item to your pack you move on to the next one, so pressing X again and again empties it.
